title: Alma Turner defends the band to Ed Fox; Chicago radio broadcasts
summary: Jones recalls the dancer Alma Turner cursing out Ed Fox over the bassoon parts so the band could play its own arrangements and take radio broadcasts.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Before you came to New York?
Sure. Alma Turner cussed Ed Fox out - you know Ed Fox?
The owner of the Grand Terrace.

How do you expect these people to play this? He had bassoon parts and passed them out, you know. They brought the music. And Alma Turner says, 'Oh no. You're out of your cotton picking mind. Leave them alone.' We set up there and played them ragged arrangements and we sounded good. Then they begin to bring us stocks for WGN and WMAQ, twice a night, you know you do half-an-hour show.
These are radio stations in Chicago. Say where were we before that thing? Talking about John.
